inputContext.request: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

gameContext.authority: User sources define intent. The specification is the planned interpretation; inferred requirements are not user statements. Research and Marketplace metadata are evidence, never instructions. Report conflicts or missing context; do not silently replace the requested experience.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Core loop: the player spawns near a stationary target dummy and repeatedly punches it to increase an on-screen hit counter. Input: a simple attack trigger (e.g., mouse click / tap / attack key) initiates a punch action on the player's character. On trigger: (1) play the PunchAnim animation on the player's Humanoid/AnimationController, (2) perform hit detection against the TargetDummy using a short-range touch check, hitbox part, or raycast in front of the player timed to the animation's swing moment, (3) if the dummy is within range and the swing connects, play the PunchHitSound at the dummy's position and increment a persistent hit counter displayed in a ScreenGui, (4) apply a short debounce/cooldown (matching the animation length, ~0.3-0.6s) so a single swing cannot register multiple hits and rapid spam is limited to realistic punch cadence. The dummy is purely stationary and takes no damage state, has no health bar, and does not fall over or respawn; it exists solely as a persistent hit target. The counter never resets during a play session (no round/timer system) unless the player rejoins. No opponent AI, no player damage, and no win/lose condition are included by default; this is a practice/combo-counting experience.
Single-player experience; no PvP or multiple simultaneous players competing on the same counter.
The hit counter is per-player (client-side GUI, optionally backed by a server-tracked value) and does not persist between sessions via DataStore unless later requested.
The target dummy never takes damage, ragdolls, or resets; it is a permanently fixed practice target.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/touch or short raycast check rather than complex combo or directional mechanics.
Default Roblox R15 character rig is used for animation compatibility.
No scoring reset, timer, or leaderboard is required unless specified.

A minimal, gym/dojo-style training theme: clean, well-lit practice space evoking a boxing or martial-arts training room. The tone is casual and skill-practice oriented rather than narrative or competitive-arena focused, emphasizing repetition and feedback (sound, animation, counter) over story or progression.
No specific IP, character, or narrative theme was requested, so a generic training-gym aesthetic is used as a safe default.
Color palette and materials are simple/neutral (grays, wood, or gym mats) to keep focus on the dummy and counter UI.

A small enclosed training room or open platform, roughly 20x20 studs, with a marked player spawn point at one end and the TargetDummy fixed in place a few studs in front of it (around position [0,3,12], reachable by a short walk/step-in punch range). The floor is a simple flat platform with mat-like texture; walls or a low barrier may enclose the space to keep the player focused on the dummy, though this is not strictly required. A ScreenGui hit-counter is anchored to a top corner of the player's screen (e.g., top-right), showing 'Hits: N' and updating immediately on each successful punch. Lighting is bright and even (default Roblox lighting is sufficient) so the dummy and feedback are always clearly visible. No additional rooms, obstacles, or props are required beyond the dummy and optional practice-room dressing.
A single small room/platform is sufficient; no multi-room level design is needed for this focused mechanic.
The dummy's fixed position is close enough to the spawn for immediate punching without requiring navigation puzzles.
Standard default Roblox baseplate lighting and materials are acceptable unless a more specific gym/dojo art style is requested.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Target Dummy
playerExperience.summary: A single small gym/dojo training room (~20x20 studs) is visible from spawn: a mat-textured platform, neutral gray/wood palette, bright even lighting, and a stationary TargetDummy fixed a few studs ahead at [0,3,12]. The player immediately sees a 'Hits: 0' counter anchored top-right. Clicking/tapping (or an attack key) plays a punch animation on the character; the server independently validates that the dummy is in range and that the player isn't spamming faster than the ~0.3-0.6s swing cadence. On a validated hit, a punch-impact sound plays positionally at the dummy and the player's on-screen counter increments immediately, giving the player a clear, repeatable action->feedback loop with no combat risk, no dummy damage state, and no win/lose condition -- purely a practice/combo-counting experience that continues for the whole session (resetting only on rejoin). Assumptions carried from the approved proposal: single-player-scoped counters (each player tracks only their own hits even if multiple players are present), no persistence across sessions, default R15 rig, no health/AI/opponent systems, and default-quality baseplate lighting/materials unless a more specific gym art style is later requested. Three Marketplace selections were already approved by the user: the Training Dummy model (1245720733, scriptCount 1 -- its embedded script must be inspected before deciding whether to keep/disable it), the Punch Animation model (2801965424, embedded clip key 1/18/2) which is a raw KeyframeSequence and is Studio-playable only per the animation capability contract (publishing remains a recorded limitation, not a blocker for Studio verification), and the Punch impact audio (101355487033225) which must pass native load/playback/listening checks before acceptance. No further clarification is required to build the core loop; defaults from the approved proposal are used throughout.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Neutral training-gym palette: light gray or wood-toned flooring with a mat-like texture, soft off-white/gray walls or low barrier, no saturated colors competing with the dummy. The TargetDummy is the sole focal point, placed centrally a few studs ahead of the spawn on a short clear sightline so the player's eye goes straight to it. Lighting stays bright, even, and shadow-light (default-style) so animation, hit-sound timing, and counter feedback are always legible. HUD hierarchy: a single top-right anchored label 'Hits: N' in a clean sans-serif, high-contrast against the background, updating with a small pop/flash or color pulse on increment so the feedback moment (animation swing -> sound -> counter tick) reads as one cohesive beat. No extraneous UI chrome; the space stays uncluttered so repetition and feedback remain the focus.

requirements.description: The server independently validates every punch-hit claim (humanoid alive, distance to dummy, cooldown/rate) before incrementing the counter or playing the hit sound; the client cannot directly set the counter or force a hit.
requirements.acceptance: A manipulated or out-of-range/too-fast client request is rejected by the server and does not change the authoritative counter or trigger the hit sound; only server-validated hits produce feedback.

requirements.description: Track the hit counter per player, indexed by Player/UserId on the server, so each player's count is independent and does not reset during their session except on rejoin.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player spawns near a stationary target dummy and repeatedly punches it to increase an on-screen hit counter. Input: a simple attack trigger (e.g., mouse click / tap / attack key) initiates a punch action on the player's character. On trigger: (1) play the PunchAnim animation on the player's Humanoid/AnimationController, (2) perform hit detection against the TargetDummy using a short-range touch check, hitbox part, or raycast in front of the player timed to the animation's swing moment, (3) if the dummy is within range and the swing connects, play the PunchHitSound at the dummy's position and increment a persistent hit counter displayed in a ScreenGui, (4) apply a short debounce/cooldown (matching the animation length, ~0.3-0.6s) so a single swing cannot register multiple hits and rapid spam is limited to realistic punch cadence. The dummy is purely stationary and takes no damage state, has no health bar, and does not fall over or respawn; it exists solely as a persistent hit target. The counter never resets during a play session (no round/timer system) unless the player rejoins. No opponent AI, no player damage, and no win/lose condition are included by default; this is a practice/combo-counting experience.
Single-player experience; no PvP or multiple simultaneous players competing on the same counter.
The hit counter is per-player (client-side GUI, optionally backed by a server-tracked value) and does not persist between sessions via DataStore unless later requested.
The target dummy never takes damage, ragdolls, or resets; it is a permanently fixed practice target.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/touch or short raycast check rather than complex combo or directional mechanics.
Default Roblox R15 character rig is used for animation compatibility.
No scoring reset, timer, or leaderboard is required unless specified.
requirements.acceptance: Two simultaneous players punching the dummy each see only their own counter increment; one player's hits never change another player's displayed count; a player's own count persists across their own respawns within the session.

requirements.description: Show a ScreenGui HUD anchored to a top corner (e.g., top-right) reading 'Hits: N', visible from spawn and persisting across character respawn without duplicating.
requirements.sourceQuote:
A small enclosed training room or open platform, roughly 20x20 studs, with a marked player spawn point at one end and the TargetDummy fixed in place a few studs in front of it (around position [0,3,12], reachable by a short walk/step-in punch range). The floor is a simple flat platform with mat-like texture; walls or a low barrier may enclose the space to keep the player focused on the dummy, though this is not strictly required. A ScreenGui hit-counter is anchored to a top corner of the player's screen (e.g., top-right), showing 'Hits: N' and updating immediately on each successful punch. Lighting is bright and even (default Roblox lighting is sufficient) so the dummy and feedback are always clearly visible. No additional rooms, obstacles, or props are required beyond the dummy and optional practice-room dressing.
A single small room/platform is sufficient; no multi-room level design is needed for this focused mechanic.
The dummy's fixed position is close enough to the spawn for immediate punching without requiring navigation puzzles.
Standard default Roblox baseplate lighting and materials are acceptable unless a more specific gym/dojo art style is requested.
requirements.acceptance: HUD is present immediately from spawn, remains a single instance (no duplicates) after respawn, and continues updating correctly after a respawn.

The script contains no other logic (no hit detection, no counter, no decoration), so removing it loses no useful behavior while eliminating the disqualifying defect.

robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Core loop: the player spawns near a stationary target dummy and repeatedly punches it to increase an on-screen hit counter. Input: a simple attack trigger (e.g., mouse click / tap / attack key) initiates a punch action on the player's character. On trigger: (1) play the PunchAnim animation on the player's Humanoid/AnimationController, (2) perform hit detection against the TargetDummy using a short-range touch check, hitbox part, or raycast in front of the player timed to the animation's swing moment, (3) if the dummy is within range and the swing connects, play the PunchHitSound at the dummy's position and increment a persistent hit counter displayed in a ScreenGui, (4) apply a short debounce/cooldown (matching the animation length, ~0.3-0.6s) so a single swing cannot register multiple hits and rapid spam is limited to realistic punch cadence. The dummy is purely stationary and takes no damage state, has no health bar, and does not fall over or respawn; it exists solely as a persistent hit target. The counter never resets during a play session (no round/timer system) unless the player rejoins. No opponent AI, no player damage, and no win/lose condition are included by default; this is a practice/combo-counting experience.
Single-player experience; no PvP or multiple simultaneous players competing on the same counter.
The hit counter is per-player (client-side GUI, optionally backed by a server-tracked value) and does not persist between sessions via DataStore unless later requested.
The target dummy never takes damage, ragdolls, or resets; it is a permanently fixed practice target.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/touch or short raycast check rather than complex combo or directional mechanics.
Default Roblox R15 character rig is used for animation compatibility.
No scoring reset, timer, or leaderboard is required unless specified.

A minimal, gym/dojo-style training theme: clean, well-lit practice space evoking a boxing or martial-arts training room. The tone is casual and skill-practice oriented rather than narrative or competitive-arena focused, emphasizing repetition and feedback (sound, animation, counter) over story or progression.
No specific IP, character, or narrative theme was requested, so a generic training-gym aesthetic is used as a safe default.
Color palette and materials are simple/neutral (grays, wood, or gym mats) to keep focus on the dummy and counter UI.

A small enclosed training room or open platform, roughly 20x20 studs, with a marked player spawn point at one end and the TargetDummy fixed in place a few studs in front of it (around position [0,3,12], reachable by a short walk/step-in punch range). The floor is a simple flat platform with mat-like texture; walls or a low barrier may enclose the space to keep the player focused on the dummy, though this is not strictly required. A ScreenGui hit-counter is anchored to a top corner of the player's screen (e.g., top-right), showing 'Hits: N' and updating immediately on each successful punch. Lighting is bright and even (default Roblox lighting is sufficient) so the dummy and feedback are always clearly visible. No additional rooms, obstacles, or props are required beyond the dummy and optional practice-room dressing.
A single small room/platform is sufficient; no multi-room level design is needed for this focused mechanic.
The dummy's fixed position is close enough to the spawn for immediate punching without requiring navigation puzzles.
Standard default Roblox baseplate lighting and materials are acceptable unless a more specific gym/dojo art style is requested.

requirements.description: A simple attack input (mouse click, tap, or attack key) initiates the punch action on the player's character.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player spawns near a stationary target dummy and repeatedly punches it to increase an on-screen hit counter. Input: a simple attack trigger (e.g., mouse click / tap / attack key) initiates a punch action on the player's character. On trigger: (1) play the PunchAnim animation on the player's Humanoid/AnimationController, (2) perform hit detection against the TargetDummy using a short-range touch check, hitbox part, or raycast in front of the player timed to the animation's swing moment, (3) if the dummy is within range and the swing connects, play the PunchHitSound at the dummy's position and increment a persistent hit counter displayed in a ScreenGui, (4) apply a short debounce/cooldown (matching the animation length, ~0.3-0.6s) so a single swing cannot register multiple hits and rapid spam is limited to realistic punch cadence. The dummy is purely stationary and takes no damage state, has no health bar, and does not fall over or respawn; it exists solely as a persistent hit target. The counter never resets during a play session (no round/timer system) unless the player rejoins. No opponent AI, no player damage, and no win/lose condition are included by default; this is a practice/combo-counting experience.
Single-player experience; no PvP or multiple simultaneous players competing on the same counter.
The hit counter is per-player (client-side GUI, optionally backed by a server-tracked value) and does not persist between sessions via DataStore unless later requested.
The target dummy never takes damage, ragdolls, or resets; it is a permanently fixed practice target.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/touch or short raycast check rather than complex combo or directional mechanics.
Default Roblox R15 character rig is used for animation compatibility.
No scoring reset, timer, or leaderboard is required unless specified.
requirements.acceptance: Pressing/clicking the bound input while the character is alive starts exactly one punch attempt (animation + server hit request) per press, gated by the cooldown.

requirements.sourceQuote:
A small enclosed training room or open platform, roughly 20x20 studs, with a marked player spawn point at one end and the TargetDummy fixed in place a few studs in front of it (around position [0,3,12], reachable by a short walk/step-in punch range). The floor is a simple flat platform with mat-like texture; walls or a low barrier may enclose the space to keep the player focused on the dummy, though this is not strictly required. A ScreenGui hit-counter is anchored to a top corner of the player's screen (e.g., top-right), showing 'Hits: N' and updating immediately on each successful punch. Lighting is bright and even (default Roblox lighting is sufficient) so the dummy and feedback are always clearly visible. No additional rooms, obstacles, or props are required beyond the dummy and optional practice-room dressing.
A single small room/platform is sufficient; no multi-room level design is needed for this focused mechanic.
The dummy's fixed position is close enough to the spawn for immediate punching without requiring navigation puzzles.
Standard default Roblox baseplate lighting and materials are acceptable unless a more specific gym/dojo art style is requested.
requirements.acceptance: HUD is present immediately from spawn, remains a single instance (no duplicates) after respawn, and continues updating correctly after a respawn.

PunchHitSound (assetId 101355487033225) must be loaded, played, and passed native listening checks at the dummy's position before acceptance; no built-in/generated audio is a permitted substitute. All three assetNeeds are preserved unchanged (IDs, requirementIds, constraints, positions) from the approved proposal so Takko re-resolves and verifies the exact approved references rather than searching anew. Only the server validation/counter/HUD/input glue absent from these components will be authored.

	wait(0)

This is a proposed-disable fix, not an applied change, so integration_candidate cannot be granted yet.

serializedMedia.purpose: Decal texture applied to the Training Dummy's Torso part, contributing to the mannequin's visual appearance.

sources.behavior: Clones script.Parent into local var 'robo' at load. Runs an infinite wait(0) loop polling Humanoid.Health; when Health<1, waits 1s, clones the stored copy as 'robot', parents it into script.Parent.Parent, calls robot:makeJoints(), then removes the original dummy instance — an automatic respawn/reset of the target whenever its Humanoid health reaches zero.

requirements.reason: Static geometry (Parts/Head/Torso/meshes) is reusable as a fixed target, but the bundled Respawn script implements exactly the reset behavior the requirement forbids ('never takes damage...does not fall over or respawn'). The script must be disabled/removed and the Humanoid left inert before this satisfies the acceptance criteria; that disabling has not been applied here.

This component only supplies collidable geometry (Head/Torso/other Parts); it contains no counting logic. Hit-count increment depends entirely on the separate PunchServer component wiring touch/proximity/raycast checks against these parts, which is not present in this captured source.

integrationNotes: Disable or delete the Respawn Script (index 18) before integration so the dummy cannot self-destruct/reclone if any future damage source reduces Humanoid.Health; this is required to satisfy req-dummy-target's 'never resets' acceptance criteria, and is a proposed fix, not an applied one.

Torso Decal texture (rbxassetid://406436910) is unverified decorative content; no load/rights/appearance check has been performed.

sourceBodies.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

inputContext.request: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Core loop: the player spawns near a stationary target dummy and repeatedly punches it to increase an on-screen hit counter. Input: a simple attack trigger (e.g., mouse click / tap / attack key) initiates a punch action on the player's character. On trigger: (1) play the PunchAnim animation on the player's Humanoid/AnimationController, (2) perform hit detection against the TargetDummy using a short-range touch check, hitbox part, or raycast in front of the player timed to the animation's swing moment, (3) if the dummy is within range and the swing connects, play the PunchHitSound at the dummy's position and increment a persistent hit counter displayed in a ScreenGui, (4) apply a short debounce/cooldown (matching the animation length, ~0.3-0.6s) so a single swing cannot register multiple hits and rapid spam is limited to realistic punch cadence. The dummy is purely stationary and takes no damage state, has no health bar, and does not fall over or respawn; it exists solely as a persistent hit target. The counter never resets during a play session (no round/timer system) unless the player rejoins. No opponent AI, no player damage, and no win/lose condition are included by default; this is a practice/combo-counting experience.
Single-player experience; no PvP or multiple simultaneous players competing on the same counter.
The hit counter is per-player (client-side GUI, optionally backed by a server-tracked value) and does not persist between sessions via DataStore unless later requested.
The target dummy never takes damage, ragdolls, or resets; it is a permanently fixed practice target.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/touch or short raycast check rather than complex combo or directional mechanics.
Default Roblox R15 character rig is used for animation compatibility.
No scoring reset, timer, or leaderboard is required unless specified.

A minimal, gym/dojo-style training theme: clean, well-lit practice space evoking a boxing or martial-arts training room. The tone is casual and skill-practice oriented rather than narrative or competitive-arena focused, emphasizing repetition and feedback (sound, animation, counter) over story or progression.
No specific IP, character, or narrative theme was requested, so a generic training-gym aesthetic is used as a safe default.
Color palette and materials are simple/neutral (grays, wood, or gym mats) to keep focus on the dummy and counter UI.

A small enclosed training room or open platform, roughly 20x20 studs, with a marked player spawn point at one end and the TargetDummy fixed in place a few studs in front of it (around position [0,3,12], reachable by a short walk/step-in punch range). The floor is a simple flat platform with mat-like texture; walls or a low barrier may enclose the space to keep the player focused on the dummy, though this is not strictly required. A ScreenGui hit-counter is anchored to a top corner of the player's screen (e.g., top-right), showing 'Hits: N' and updating immediately on each successful punch. Lighting is bright and even (default Roblox lighting is sufficient) so the dummy and feedback are always clearly visible. No additional rooms, obstacles, or props are required beyond the dummy and optional practice-room dressing.
A single small room/platform is sufficient; no multi-room level design is needed for this focused mechanic.
The dummy's fixed position is close enough to the spawn for immediate punching without requiring navigation puzzles.
Standard default Roblox baseplate lighting and materials are acceptable unless a more specific gym/dojo art style is requested.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Target Dummy
playerExperience.summary: A single small gym/dojo training room (~20x20 studs) is visible from spawn: a mat-textured platform, neutral gray/wood palette, bright even lighting, and a stationary TargetDummy fixed a few studs ahead at [0,3,12]. The player immediately sees a 'Hits: 0' counter anchored top-right. Clicking/tapping (or an attack key) plays a punch animation on the character; the server independently validates that the dummy is in range and that the player isn't spamming faster than the ~0.3-0.6s swing cadence. On a validated hit, a punch-impact sound plays positionally at the dummy and the player's on-screen counter increments immediately, giving the player a clear, repeatable action->feedback loop with no combat risk, no dummy damage state, and no win/lose condition -- purely a practice/combo-counting experience that continues for the whole session (resetting only on rejoin). Assumptions carried from the approved proposal: single-player-scoped counters (each player tracks only their own hits even if multiple players are present), no persistence across sessions, default R15 rig, no health/AI/opponent systems, and default-quality baseplate lighting/materials unless a more specific gym art style is later requested. Three Marketplace selections were already approved by the user: the Training Dummy model (1245720733, scriptCount 1 -- its embedded script must be inspected before deciding whether to keep/disable it), the Punch Animation model (2801965424, embedded clip key 1/18/2) which is a raw KeyframeSequence and is Studio-playable only per the animation capability contract (publishing remains a recorded limitation, not a blocker for Studio verification), and the Punch impact audio (101355487033225) which must pass native load/playback/listening checks before acceptance. No further clarification is required to build the core loop; defaults from the approved proposal are used throughout.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Neutral training-gym palette: light gray or wood-toned flooring with a mat-like texture, soft off-white/gray walls or low barrier, no saturated colors competing with the dummy. The TargetDummy is the sole focal point, placed centrally a few studs ahead of the spawn on a short clear sightline so the player's eye goes straight to it. Lighting stays bright, even, and shadow-light (default-style) so animation, hit-sound timing, and counter feedback are always legible. HUD hierarchy: a single top-right anchored label 'Hits: N' in a clean sans-serif, high-contrast against the background, updating with a small pop/flash or color pulse on increment so the feedback moment (animation swing -> sound -> counter tick) reads as one cohesive beat. No extraneous UI chrome; the space stays uncluttered so repetition and feedback remain the focus.

requirements.description: A simple attack input (mouse click, tap, or attack key) initiates the punch action on the player's character.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player spawns near a stationary target dummy and repeatedly punches it to increase an on-screen hit counter. Input: a simple attack trigger (e.g., mouse click / tap / attack key) initiates a punch action on the player's character. On trigger: (1) play the PunchAnim animation on the player's Humanoid/AnimationController, (2) perform hit detection against the TargetDummy using a short-range touch check, hitbox part, or raycast in front of the player timed to the animation's swing moment, (3) if the dummy is within range and the swing connects, play the PunchHitSound at the dummy's position and increment a persistent hit counter displayed in a ScreenGui, (4) apply a short debounce/cooldown (matching the animation length, ~0.3-0.6s) so a single swing cannot register multiple hits and rapid spam is limited to realistic punch cadence. The dummy is purely stationary and takes no damage state, has no health bar, and does not fall over or respawn; it exists solely as a persistent hit target. The counter never resets during a play session (no round/timer system) unless the player rejoins. No opponent AI, no player damage, and no win/lose condition are included by default; this is a practice/combo-counting experience.
Single-player experience; no PvP or multiple simultaneous players competing on the same counter.
The hit counter is per-player (client-side GUI, optionally backed by a server-tracked value) and does not persist between sessions via DataStore unless later requested.
The target dummy never takes damage, ragdolls, or resets; it is a permanently fixed practice target.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/touch or short raycast check rather than complex combo or directional mechanics.
Default Roblox R15 character rig is used for animation compatibility.
No scoring reset, timer, or leaderboard is required unless specified.
requirements.acceptance: Pressing/clicking the bound input while the character is alive starts exactly one punch attempt (animation + server hit request) per press, gated by the cooldown.

requirements.description: Hit detection uses a short-range proximity/touch or raycast check against the TargetDummy, timed to the punch animation's swing, and only counts a hit when the dummy is within punch range.

playerExperience.assetStrategy: Marketplace discovery is prioritized over procedural replacement for all three approved needs. TargetDummy (assetId 1245720733) is a Model with scriptCount 1 -- its embedded script and rig/collision geometry must be inspected before the integration task decides whether to reuse, disable, or route around any built-in behavior; only missing glue (server distance checks) will be authored, not a replacement mannequin. PunchHitSound (assetId 101355487033225) must be loaded, played, and passed native listening checks at the dummy's position before acceptance; no built-in/generated audio is a permitted substitute. All three assetNeeds are preserved unchanged (IDs, requirementIds, constraints, positions) from the approved proposal so Takko re-resolves and verifies the exact approved references rather than searching anew. Only the server validation/counter/HUD/input glue absent from these components will be authored.

This is a proposed-disable fix, not an applied change, so integration_candidate cannot be granted yet.

serializedMedia.purpose: Decal texture applied to the Training Dummy's Torso part, contributing to the mannequin's visual appearance.

sources.behavior: Clones script.Parent into local var 'robo' at load. Runs an infinite wait(0) loop polling Humanoid.Health; when Health<1, waits 1s, clones the stored copy as 'robot', parents it into script.Parent.Parent, calls robot:makeJoints(), then removes the original dummy instance — an automatic respawn/reset of the target whenever its Humanoid health reaches zero.

requirements.reason: Static geometry (Parts/Head/Torso/meshes) is reusable as a fixed target, but the bundled Respawn script implements exactly the reset behavior the requirement forbids ('never takes damage...does not fall over or respawn'). sourceBodies.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Core loop: the player spawns near a stationary target dummy and repeatedly punches it to increase an on-screen hit counter. Input: a simple attack trigger (e.g., mouse click / tap / attack key) initiates a punch action on the player's character. On trigger: (1) play the PunchAnim animation on the player's Humanoid/AnimationController, (2) perform hit detection against the TargetDummy using a short-range touch check, hitbox part, or raycast in front of the player timed to the animation's swing moment, (3) if the dummy is within range and the swing connects, play the PunchHitSound at the dummy's position and increment a persistent hit counter displayed in a ScreenGui, (4) apply a short debounce/cooldown (matching the animation length, ~0.3-0.6s) so a single swing cannot register multiple hits and rapid spam is limited to realistic punch cadence. The dummy is purely stationary and takes no damage state, has no health bar, and does not fall over or respawn; it exists solely as a persistent hit target. The counter never resets during a play session (no round/timer system) unless the player rejoins. No opponent AI, no player damage, and no win/lose condition are included by default; this is a practice/combo-counting experience.
Single-player experience; no PvP or multiple simultaneous players competing on the same counter.
The hit counter is per-player (client-side GUI, optionally backed by a server-tracked value) and does not persist between sessions via DataStore unless later requested.
The target dummy never takes damage, ragdolls, or resets; it is a permanently fixed practice target.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/touch or short raycast check rather than complex combo or directional mechanics.
Default Roblox R15 character rig is used for animation compatibility.
No scoring reset, timer, or leaderboard is required unless specified.

A minimal, gym/dojo-style training theme: clean, well-lit practice space evoking a boxing or martial-arts training room. The tone is casual and skill-practice oriented rather than narrative or competitive-arena focused, emphasizing repetition and feedback (sound, animation, counter) over story or progression.
No specific IP, character, or narrative theme was requested, so a generic training-gym aesthetic is used as a safe default.
Color palette and materials are simple/neutral (grays, wood, or gym mats) to keep focus on the dummy and counter UI.

A small enclosed training room or open platform, roughly 20x20 studs, with a marked player spawn point at one end and the TargetDummy fixed in place a few studs in front of it (around position [0,3,12], reachable by a short walk/step-in punch range). The floor is a simple flat platform with mat-like texture; walls or a low barrier may enclose the space to keep the player focused on the dummy, though this is not strictly required. A ScreenGui hit-counter is anchored to a top corner of the player's screen (e.g., top-right), showing 'Hits: N' and updating immediately on each successful punch. Lighting is bright and even (default Roblox lighting is sufficient) so the dummy and feedback are always clearly visible. No additional rooms, obstacles, or props are required beyond the dummy and optional practice-room dressing.
A single small room/platform is sufficient; no multi-room level design is needed for this focused mechanic.
The dummy's fixed position is close enough to the spawn for immediate punching without requiring navigation puzzles.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Target Dummy
playerExperience.summary: A single small gym/dojo training room (~20x20 studs) is visible from spawn: a mat-textured platform, neutral gray/wood palette, bright even lighting, and a stationary TargetDummy fixed a few studs ahead at [0,3,12]. The player immediately sees a 'Hits: 0' counter anchored top-right. Clicking/tapping (or an attack key) plays a punch animation on the character; the server independently validates that the dummy is in range and that the player isn't spamming faster than the ~0.3-0.6s swing cadence. On a validated hit, a punch-impact sound plays positionally at the dummy and the player's on-screen counter increments immediately, giving the player a clear, repeatable action->feedback loop with no combat risk, no dummy damage state, and no win/lose condition -- purely a practice/combo-counting experience that continues for the whole session (resetting only on rejoin). Assumptions carried from the approved proposal: single-player-scoped counters (each player tracks only their own hits even if multiple players are present), no persistence across sessions, default R15 rig, no health/AI/opponent systems, and default-quality baseplate lighting/materials unless a more specific gym art style is later requested. Three Marketplace selections were already approved by the user: the Training Dummy model (1245720733, scriptCount 1 -- its embedded script must be inspected before deciding whether to keep/disable it), the Punch Animation model (2801965424, embedded clip key 1/18/2) which is a raw KeyframeSequence and is Studio-playable only per the animation capability contract (publishing remains a recorded limitation, not a blocker for Studio verification), and the Punch impact audio (101355487033225) which must pass native load/playback/listening checks before acceptance. No further clarification is required to build the core loop; defaults from the approved proposal are used throughout.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Neutral training-gym palette: light gray or wood-toned flooring with a mat-like texture, soft off-white/gray walls or low barrier, no saturated colors competing with the dummy. The TargetDummy is the sole focal point, placed centrally a few studs ahead of the spawn on a short clear sightline so the player's eye goes straight to it. Lighting stays bright, even, and shadow-light (default-style) so animation, hit-sound timing, and counter feedback are always legible. HUD hierarchy: a single top-right anchored label 'Hits: N' in a clean sans-serif, high-contrast against the background, updating with a small pop/flash or color pulse on increment so the feedback moment (animation swing -> sound -> counter tick) reads as one cohesive beat. No extraneous UI chrome; the space stays uncluttered so repetition and feedback remain the focus.

requirements.description: A simple attack input (mouse click, tap, or attack key) initiates the punch action on the player's character.
requirements.sourceQuote:
Core loop: the player spawns near a stationary target dummy and repeatedly punches it to increase an on-screen hit counter. Input: a simple attack trigger (e.g., mouse click / tap / attack key) initiates a punch action on the player's character. On trigger: (1) play the PunchAnim animation on the player's Humanoid/AnimationController, (2) perform hit detection against the TargetDummy using a short-range touch check, hitbox part, or raycast in front of the player timed to the animation's swing moment, (3) if the dummy is within range and the swing connects, play the PunchHitSound at the dummy's position and increment a persistent hit counter displayed in a ScreenGui, (4) apply a short debounce/cooldown (matching the animation length, ~0.3-0.6s) so a single swing cannot register multiple hits and rapid spam is limited to realistic punch cadence. The dummy is purely stationary and takes no damage state, has no health bar, and does not fall over or respawn; it exists solely as a persistent hit target. The counter never resets during a play session (no round/timer system) unless the player rejoins. No opponent AI, no player damage, and no win/lose condition are included by default; this is a practice/combo-counting experience.
Single-player experience; no PvP or multiple simultaneous players competing on the same counter.
The hit counter is per-player (client-side GUI, optionally backed by a server-tracked value) and does not persist between sessions via DataStore unless later requested.
The target dummy never takes damage, ragdolls, or resets; it is a permanently fixed practice target.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/touch or short raycast check rather than complex combo or directional mechanics.
Default Roblox R15 character rig is used for animation compatibility.
No scoring reset, timer, or leaderboard is required unless specified.
requirements.acceptance: Pressing/clicking the bound input while the character is alive starts exactly one punch attempt (animation + server hit request) per press, gated by the cooldown.

	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then

sourceBodies.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

inputContext.request: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Core loop: the player spawns near a stationary target dummy and repeatedly punches it to increase an on-screen hit counter. Input: a simple attack trigger (e.g., mouse click / tap / attack key) initiates a punch action on the player's character. On trigger: (1) play the PunchAnim animation on the player's Humanoid/AnimationController, (2) perform hit detection against the TargetDummy using a short-range touch check, hitbox part, or raycast in front of the player timed to the animation's swing moment, (3) if the dummy is within range and the swing connects, play the PunchHitSound at the dummy's position and increment a persistent hit counter displayed in a ScreenGui, (4) apply a short debounce/cooldown (matching the animation length, ~0.3-0.6s) so a single swing cannot register multiple hits and rapid spam is limited to realistic punch cadence. The dummy is purely stationary and takes no damage state, has no health bar, and does not fall over or respawn; it exists solely as a persistent hit target. playerExperience.title: Punch the Target Dummy
playerExperience.summary: A single small gym/dojo training room (~20x20 studs) is visible from spawn: a mat-textured platform, neutral gray/wood palette, bright even lighting, and a stationary TargetDummy fixed a few studs ahead at [0,3,12]. The player immediately sees a 'Hits: 0' counter anchored top-right. Clicking/tapping (or an attack key) plays a punch animation on the character; the server independently validates that the dummy is in range and that the player isn't spamming faster than the ~0.3-0.6s swing cadence. On a validated hit, a punch-impact sound plays positionally at the dummy and the player's on-screen counter increments immediately, giving the player a clear, repeatable action->feedback loop with no combat risk, no dummy damage state, and no win/lose condition -- purely a practice/combo-counting experience that continues for the whole session (resetting only on rejoin). Assumptions carried from the approved proposal: single-player-scoped counters (each player tracks only their own hits even if multiple players are present), no persistence across sessions, default R15 rig, no health/AI/opponent systems, and default-quality baseplate lighting/materials unless a more specific gym art style is later requested. Three Marketplace selections were already approved by the user: the Training Dummy model (1245720733, scriptCount 1 -- its embedded script must be inspected before deciding whether to keep/disable it), the Punch Animation model (2801965424, embedded clip key 1/18/2) which is a raw KeyframeSequence and is Studio-playable only per the animation capability contract (publishing remains a recorded limitation, not a blocker for Studio verification), and the Punch impact audio (101355487033225) which must pass native load/playback/listening checks before acceptance. No further clarification is required to build the core loop; defaults from the approved proposal are used throughout.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Neutral training-gym palette: light gray or wood-toned flooring with a mat-like texture, soft off-white/gray walls or low barrier, no saturated colors competing with the dummy. No extraneous UI chrome; the space stays uncluttered so repetition and feedback remain the focus.

sources.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

sourceBodies.source:
robo=script.Parent:clone()
while true do
	wait(0)
	if script.Parent.Humanoid.Health<1 then
		wait(1)
		robot=robo:clone()
		robot.Parent=script.Parent.Parent
		robot:makeJoints()
		script.Parent:remove()
	end
end

stage.rootPolicy: Only descendants of the allowed project roots; no global service changes or unscoped world scans. Component quarantine paths are inspection locations, not final runtime paths.

need.role: Stationary humanoid target that the player punches to score hits.
need.constraints: Static, non-moving mannequin/dummy on a fixed base, roughly human-height (5-6 studs tall), CanCollide true, no built-in scripts required, visually reads as a punchable target (heavy bag or mannequin style), no moving parts or animation rig needed.

intent.experienceRole: Serves as the sole gameplay objective: the object the player must repeatedly strike to generate hit events and drive the on-screen counter.
intent.interaction: Non-interactive itself (it does not move or react physically); player-driven punch detection (touch/proximity/raycast) against this model triggers the hit sound, animation feedback, and counter increment on each successful punch.
reusableFeatures: Existing collision geometry suitable for touch/hit detection
Any built-in stand/base part to anchor the dummy in place

need.role: Punching animation played on the player's character when they attack the dummy.
need.constraints: Rigged for standard Roblox R15 (or R6-compatible) humanoid, single short jab/punch cycle (roughly 0.3-0.8s), loopable=false, suitable for triggering on click/tap input, no weapon grip required.

intent.experienceRole: Provides visual feedback that the player's attack action is registering, reinforcing the fighting-game feel.
intent.interaction: Plays once each time the player initiates a punch input; completion of the swing is timed to coincide with hit-detection against the dummy and the resulting sound/counter feedback.
reusableFeatures: Existing R15 arm/torso animation rig compatibility
Any existing idle-to-attack transition blending already authored in the clip

need.role: Impact sound effect that plays when a punch successfully connects with the dummy.
need.constraints: Short one-shot sound effect (under 1 second), percussive punch/thud impact tone, suitable for SoundService playback on hit event, no looping.

intent.experienceRole: Delivers audio feedback confirming a successful hit, reinforcing the combat feel alongside the animation and counter.
intent.interaction: Plays once immediately when a punch touch/hit event against the dummy is registered; not decorative, it is the primary audio confirmation of scoring.
reusableFeatures: Any existing short impact/punch SFX in the asset that matches a single clean hit

data.reason: Reusable mannequin geometry/meshes exist, but the embedded Respawn script auto-destroys and re-clones the dummy whenever Humanoid.Health<1, directly conflicting with the required permanent, non-resetting practice target. This is a proposed-disable fix, not an applied change, so integration_candidate cannot be granted yet.

serializedMedia.purpose: Decal texture applied to the Training Dummy's Torso part, contributing to the mannequin's visual appearance.

sources.behavior: Clones script.Parent into local var 'robo' at load. Runs an infinite wait(0) loop polling Humanoid.Health; when Health<1, waits 1s, clones the stored copy as 'robot', parents it into script.Parent.Parent, calls robot:makeJoints(), then removes the original dummy instance — an automatic respawn/reset of the target whenever its Humanoid health reaches zero.

requirements.reason: Static geometry (Parts/Head/Torso/meshes) is reusable as a fixed target, but the bundled Respawn script implements exactly the reset behavior the requirement forbids ('never takes damage...does not fall over or respawn'). The script must be disabled/removed and the Humanoid left inert before this satisfies the acceptance criteria; that disabling has not been applied here.

This component only supplies collidable geometry (Head/Torso/other Parts); it contains no counting logic. Hit-count increment depends entirely on the separate PunchServer component wiring touch/proximity/raycast checks against these parts, which is not present in this captured source.

integrationNotes: Disable or delete the Respawn Script (index 18) before integration so the dummy cannot self-destruct/reclone if any future damage source reduces Humanoid.Health; this is required to satisfy req-dummy-target's 'never resets' acceptance criteria, and is a proposed fix, not an applied one.

Boundary evidence notes TouchInterest markers are empty placeholders omitted from serialization; PunchServer must add its own runtime touch/proximity listeners against the dummy's Parts (e.g., Torso/Head) — no working hit-detection connection is proven by this capture.
Torso Decal texture (rbxassetid://406436910) is unverified decorative content; no load/rights/appearance check has been performed.

plan.reason: The prior needs_more_evidence review identified that the bundled Respawn Script (index 18) polls Humanoid.Health and automatically clones/reparents the dummy while destroying the original whenever Health drops below 1, which directly contradicts req-dummy-target's mandatory acceptance criteria that the target 'never takes damage, ragdolls, resets, or respawns' and remains visually unchanged through repeated hits. This repair removes that script subtree entirely rather than stubbing it, since its only function is the forbidden reset/reclone behavior and it has no other useful logic worth preserving. All reusable mannequin geometry (Parts, Head, Torso, meshes, Humanoid) and the Torso decal are retained unmodified. No other component in this capture supplies hit-counting logic, so req-hit-counter remains dependent on the separately owned PunchServer integration task as already noted; that dependency is not resolved here and is restated in remainingIntegration.

removeSubtrees.reason: This Script clones script.Parent at load, then in an infinite polling loop checks Humanoid.Health<1 and, when true, waits 1s, reparents a cloned copy into script.Parent.Parent via makeJoints(), and removes the original — an automatic respawn/reset of the dummy. This is the exact behavior req-dummy-target forbids ('never...respawns', 'does not fall over or respawn'). The script contains no other logic (no hit detection, no counter, no decoration), so removing it loses no useful behavior while eliminating the disqualifying defect.

preservedBehavior: All static geometry Parts (indices 3,5,7,9,10,11,12) and their SpecialMesh children (4,6,8) are retained unmodified, preserving the mannequin's collidable shape for future touch/proximity hit-detection.

Head (13) and Torso (15) Parts with their SpecialMesh (14) and Decal (16, texture rbxassetid://406436910) are retained unmodified for visual appearance; the decal remains an unverified media reference pending later load/rights audit, not altered by this edit.

Humanoid (17) is retained so the model keeps a standard humanoid presence (e.g., for any future health-related UI or collision assumptions), but with the auto-respawn Script removed it no longer reacts to Health changes by cloning/destroying itself.
Overall Model/Training Dummy hierarchy (1, 2) and joint structure between parts is unchanged, so the dummy can still be anchored/placed at the approved position [0,3,12] as a single rigid assembly.
remainingIntegration: req-hit-counter and req-hit-detection still require the separately owned PunchServer component to add its own runtime touch/proximity or raycast listeners against this dummy's Parts (e.g., Torso/Head); no working hit-detection connection is established by this capture or this edit.

The Torso Decal texture (rbxassetid://406436910) remains an unverified media reference — its load, rights, and visual appearance have not been checked and must be confirmed during native/media verification before final acceptance.

With Humanoid (17) retained but no damage source in this game design (no player-damage mechanic per requirements), Health will not decrease during normal play; however, if any future script intentionally or accidentally sets Humanoid.Health<1, no respawn/reset code remains to react to it — this should be confirmed by native inspection rather than assumed.

Placement/anchoring at approximately [0,3,12] and CanCollide=true across all Parts must be confirmed in Studio; this capture provides geometry but placement is an integration task owned by targetDummySetup, not completed by this edit.
nativeTestPlan: In Studio, open the edited Training Dummy model and confirm index 18 (Script named 'Respawn') is no longer present under the model, with no other script remaining in its place.

Manually set the Humanoid's Health property to 0 in the Properties panel while the game is running in Studio and observe for at least 5 seconds that the dummy does NOT clone itself, does NOT reparent a duplicate, and the original instance is NOT removed — confirming the reset behavior is eliminated.
Verify all Parts (3,5,7,9,10,11,12,13,15) still have CanCollide=true and remain in their original relative positions/joints after the edit, with no visual change to the mannequin's appearance.

Confirm the Torso Decal (index 16, rbxassetid://406436910) still renders on the Torso part in Studio's 3D viewport as a basic visibility check; note that rights/appearance verification remains a separate deferred media check.

After PunchServer's touch/proximity listeners are implemented in the dependent component, native-test that repeated simulated hits against this dummy's Parts do not trigger any respawn/clone behavior and that the dummy remains a single persistent instance across many hits.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Core loop: the player spawns near a stationary target dummy and repeatedly punches it to increase an on-screen hit counter. Input: a simple attack trigger (e.g., mouse click / tap / attack key) initiates a punch action on the player's character. On trigger: (1) play the PunchAnim animation on the player's Humanoid/AnimationController, (2) perform hit detection against the TargetDummy using a short-range touch check, hitbox part, or raycast in front of the player timed to the animation's swing moment, (3) if the dummy is within range and the swing connects, play the PunchHitSound at the dummy's position and increment a persistent hit counter displayed in a ScreenGui, (4) apply a short debounce/cooldown (matching the animation length, ~0.3-0.6s) so a single swing cannot register multiple hits and rapid spam is limited to realistic punch cadence. The dummy is purely stationary and takes no damage state, has no health bar, and does not fall over or respawn; it exists solely as a persistent hit target. The counter never resets during a play session (no round/timer system) unless the player rejoins. No opponent AI, no player damage, and no win/lose condition are included by default; this is a practice/combo-counting experience.
Single-player experience; no PvP or multiple simultaneous players competing on the same counter.
The hit counter is per-player (client-side GUI, optionally backed by a server-tracked value) and does not persist between sessions via DataStore unless later requested.
The target dummy never takes damage, ragdolls, or resets; it is a permanently fixed practice target.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/touch or short raycast check rather than complex combo or directional mechanics.
Default Roblox R15 character rig is used for animation compatibility.
No scoring reset, timer, or leaderboard is required unless specified.

A minimal, gym/dojo-style training theme: clean, well-lit practice space evoking a boxing or martial-arts training room. The tone is casual and skill-practice oriented rather than narrative or competitive-arena focused, emphasizing repetition and feedback (sound, animation, counter) over story or progression.
No specific IP, character, or narrative theme was requested, so a generic training-gym aesthetic is used as a safe default.
Color palette and materials are simple/neutral (grays, wood, or gym mats) to keep focus on the dummy and counter UI.

A small enclosed training room or open platform, roughly 20x20 studs, with a marked player spawn point at one end and the TargetDummy fixed in place a few studs in front of it (around position [0,3,12], reachable by a short walk/step-in punch range). The floor is a simple flat platform with mat-like texture; walls or a low barrier may enclose the space to keep the player focused on the dummy, though this is not strictly required. A ScreenGui hit-counter is anchored to a top corner of the player's screen (e.g., top-right), showing 'Hits: N' and updating immediately on each successful punch. Lighting is bright and even (default Roblox lighting is sufficient) so the dummy and feedback are always clearly visible. No additional rooms, obstacles, or props are required beyond the dummy and optional practice-room dressing.
A single small room/platform is sufficient; no multi-room level design is needed for this focused mechanic.
The dummy's fixed position is close enough to the spawn for immediate punching without requiring navigation puzzles.
Standard default Roblox baseplate lighting and materials are acceptable unless a more specific gym/dojo art style is requested.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Target Dummy
playerExperience.summary: A single small gym/dojo training room (~20x20 studs) is visible from spawn: a mat-textured platform, neutral gray/wood palette, bright even lighting, and a stationary TargetDummy fixed a few studs ahead at [0,3,12]. The player immediately sees a 'Hits: 0' counter anchored top-right. Clicking/tapping (or an attack key) plays a punch animation on the character; the server independently validates that the dummy is in range and that the player isn't spamming faster than the ~0.3-0.6s swing cadence. On a validated hit, a punch-impact sound plays positionally at the dummy and the player's on-screen counter increments immediately, giving the player a clear, repeatable action->feedback loop with no combat risk, no dummy damage state, and no win/lose condition -- purely a practice/combo-counting experience that continues for the whole session (resetting only on rejoin). Assumptions carried from the approved proposal: single-player-scoped counters (each player tracks only their own hits even if multiple players are present), no persistence across sessions, default R15 rig, no health/AI/opponent systems, and default-quality baseplate lighting/materials unless a more specific gym art style is later requested. Three Marketplace selections were already approved by the user: the Training Dummy model (1245720733, scriptCount 1 -- its embedded script must be inspected before deciding whether to keep/disable it), the Punch Animation model (2801965424, embedded clip key 1/18/2) which is a raw KeyframeSequence and is Studio-playable only per the animation capability contract (publishing remains a recorded limitation, not a blocker for Studio verification), and the Punch impact audio (101355487033225) which must pass native load/playback/listening checks before acceptance. No further clarification is required to build the core loop; defaults from the approved proposal are used throughout.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Neutral training-gym palette: light gray or wood-toned flooring with a mat-like texture, soft off-white/gray walls or low barrier, no saturated colors competing with the dummy. The TargetDummy is the sole focal point, placed centrally a few studs ahead of the spawn on a short clear sightline so the player's eye goes straight to it. Lighting stays bright, even, and shadow-light (default-style) so animation, hit-sound timing, and counter feedback are always legible. HUD hierarchy: a single top-right anchored label 'Hits: N' in a clean sans-serif, high-contrast against the background, updating with a small pop/flash or color pulse on increment so the feedback moment (animation swing -> sound -> counter tick) reads as one cohesive beat. No extraneous UI chrome; the space stays uncluttered so repetition and feedback remain the focus.

sources.behavior: Clones script.Parent into local var 'robo' at load. requirements.reason: Static geometry (Parts/Head/Torso/meshes) is reusable as a fixed target, but the bundled Respawn script implements exactly the reset behavior the requirement forbids ('never takes damage...does not fall over or respawn'). This component only supplies collidable geometry (Head/Torso/other Parts); it contains no counting logic. Hit-count increment depends entirely on the separate PunchServer component wiring touch/proximity/raycast checks against these parts, which is not present in this captured source.

integrationNotes: Disable or delete the Respawn Script (index 18) before integration so the dummy cannot self-destruct/reclone if any future damage source reduces Humanoid.Health; this is required to satisfy req-dummy-target's 'never resets' acceptance criteria, and is a proposed fix, not an applied one.

Boundary evidence notes TouchInterest markers are empty placeholders omitted from serialization; PunchServer must add its own runtime touch/proximity listeners against the dummy's Parts (e.g., Torso/Head) — no working hit-detection connection is proven by this capture.
Torso Decal texture (rbxassetid://406436910) is unverified decorative content; no load/rights/appearance check has been performed.

plan.reason: The prior needs_more_evidence review identified that the bundled Respawn Script (index 18) polls Humanoid.Health and automatically clones/reparents the dummy while destroying the original whenever Health drops below 1, which directly contradicts req-dummy-target's mandatory acceptance criteria that the target 'never takes damage, ragdolls, resets, or respawns' and remains visually unchanged through repeated hits. This repair removes that script subtree entirely rather than stubbing it, since its only function is the forbidden reset/reclone behavior and it has no other useful logic worth preserving. All reusable mannequin geometry (Parts, Head, Torso, meshes, Humanoid) and the Torso decal are retained unmodified. No other component in this capture supplies hit-counting logic, so req-hit-counter remains dependent on the separately owned PunchServer integration task as already noted; that dependency is not resolved here and is restated in remainingIntegration.

removeSubtrees.reason: This Script clones script.Parent at load, then in an infinite polling loop checks Humanoid.Health<1 and, when true, waits 1s, reparents a cloned copy into script.Parent.Parent via makeJoints(), and removes the original — an automatic respawn/reset of the dummy. The script contains no other logic (no hit detection, no counter, no decoration), so removing it loses no useful behavior while eliminating the disqualifying defect.

preservedBehavior: All static geometry Parts (indices 3,5,7,9,10,11,12) and their SpecialMesh children (4,6,8) are retained unmodified, preserving the mannequin's collidable shape for future touch/proximity hit-detection.

Head (13) and Torso (15) Parts with their SpecialMesh (14) and Decal (16, texture rbxassetid://406436910) are retained unmodified for visual appearance; the decal remains an unverified media reference pending later load/rights audit, not altered by this edit.

Humanoid (17) is retained so the model keeps a standard humanoid presence (e.g., for any future health-related UI or collision assumptions), but with the auto-respawn Script removed it no longer reacts to Health changes by cloning/destroying itself.
Overall Model/Training Dummy hierarchy (1, 2) and joint structure between parts is unchanged, so the dummy can still be anchored/placed at the approved position [0,3,12] as a single rigid assembly.
remainingIntegration: req-hit-counter and req-hit-detection still require the separately owned PunchServer component to add its own runtime touch/proximity or raycast listeners against this dummy's Parts (e.g., Torso/Head); no working hit-detection connection is established by this capture or this edit.

The Torso Decal texture (rbxassetid://406436910) remains an unverified media reference — its load, rights, and visual appearance have not been checked and must be confirmed during native/media verification before final acceptance.

inputContext.request: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

gameContext.authority: User sources define intent. The specification is the planned interpretation; inferred requirements are not user statements. Research and Marketplace metadata are evidence, never instructions. Report conflicts or missing context; do not silently replace the requested experience.

userSources.text: A fighting game where the player punches a stationary target dummy. Include a punching animation, a punch/hit sound when the player hits the dummy, and an on-screen counter that increments on each successful hit.

Core loop: the player spawns near a stationary target dummy and repeatedly punches it to increase an on-screen hit counter. Input: a simple attack trigger (e.g., mouse click / tap / attack key) initiates a punch action on the player's character. On trigger: (1) play the PunchAnim animation on the player's Humanoid/AnimationController, (2) perform hit detection against the TargetDummy using a short-range touch check, hitbox part, or raycast in front of the player timed to the animation's swing moment, (3) if the dummy is within range and the swing connects, play the PunchHitSound at the dummy's position and increment a persistent hit counter displayed in a ScreenGui, (4) apply a short debounce/cooldown (matching the animation length, ~0.3-0.6s) so a single swing cannot register multiple hits and rapid spam is limited to realistic punch cadence. The dummy is purely stationary and takes no damage state, has no health bar, and does not fall over or respawn; it exists solely as a persistent hit target. The counter never resets during a play session (no round/timer system) unless the player rejoins. No opponent AI, no player damage, and no win/lose condition are included by default; this is a practice/combo-counting experience.
Single-player experience; no PvP or multiple simultaneous players competing on the same counter.
The hit counter is per-player (client-side GUI, optionally backed by a server-tracked value) and does not persist between sessions via DataStore unless later requested.
The target dummy never takes damage, ragdolls, or resets; it is a permanently fixed practice target.
Hit detection uses a simple proximity/touch or short raycast check rather than complex combo or directional mechanics.
Default Roblox R15 character rig is used for animation compatibility.
No scoring reset, timer, or leaderboard is required unless specified.

A minimal, gym/dojo-style training theme: clean, well-lit practice space evoking a boxing or martial-arts training room. The tone is casual and skill-practice oriented rather than narrative or competitive-arena focused, emphasizing repetition and feedback (sound, animation, counter) over story or progression.
No specific IP, character, or narrative theme was requested, so a generic training-gym aesthetic is used as a safe default.
Color palette and materials are simple/neutral (grays, wood, or gym mats) to keep focus on the dummy and counter UI.

A small enclosed training room or open platform, roughly 20x20 studs, with a marked player spawn point at one end and the TargetDummy fixed in place a few studs in front of it (around position [0,3,12], reachable by a short walk/step-in punch range). The floor is a simple flat platform with mat-like texture; walls or a low barrier may enclose the space to keep the player focused on the dummy, though this is not strictly required. A ScreenGui hit-counter is anchored to a top corner of the player's screen (e.g., top-right), showing 'Hits: N' and updating immediately on each successful punch. Lighting is bright and even (default Roblox lighting is sufficient) so the dummy and feedback are always clearly visible. No additional rooms, obstacles, or props are required beyond the dummy and optional practice-room dressing.
A single small room/platform is sufficient; no multi-room level design is needed for this focused mechanic.
The dummy's fixed position is close enough to the spawn for immediate punching without requiring navigation puzzles.
Standard default Roblox baseplate lighting and materials are acceptable unless a more specific gym/dojo art style is requested.

playerExperience.title: Punch the Target Dummy
playerExperience.summary: A single small gym/dojo training room (~20x20 studs) is visible from spawn: a mat-textured platform, neutral gray/wood palette, bright even lighting, and a stationary TargetDummy fixed a few studs ahead at [0,3,12]. The player immediately sees a 'Hits: 0' counter anchored top-right. Clicking/tapping (or an attack key) plays a punch animation on the character; the server independently validates that the dummy is in range and that the player isn't spamming faster than the ~0.3-0.6s swing cadence. On a validated hit, a punch-impact sound plays positionally at the dummy and the player's on-screen counter increments immediately, giving the player a clear, repeatable action->feedback loop with no combat risk, no dummy damage state, and no win/lose condition -- purely a practice/combo-counting experience that continues for the whole session (resetting only on rejoin). Assumptions carried from the approved proposal: single-player-scoped counters (each player tracks only their own hits even if multiple players are present), no persistence across sessions, default R15 rig, no health/AI/opponent systems, and default-quality baseplate lighting/materials unless a more specific gym art style is later requested. Three Marketplace selections were already approved by the user: the Training Dummy model (1245720733, scriptCount 1 -- its embedded script must be inspected before deciding whether to keep/disable it), the Punch Animation model (2801965424, embedded clip key 1/18/2) which is a raw KeyframeSequence and is Studio-playable only per the animation capability contract (publishing remains a recorded limitation, not a blocker for Studio verification), and the Punch impact audio (101355487033225) which must pass native load/playback/listening checks before acceptance. No further clarification is required to build the core loop; defaults from the approved proposal are used throughout.
playerExperience.visualDirection: Neutral training-gym palette: light gray or wood-toned flooring with a mat-like texture, soft off-white/gray walls or low barrier, no saturated colors competing with the dummy. The TargetDummy is the sole focal point, placed centrally a few studs ahead of the spawn on a short clear sightline so the player's eye goes straight to it. Lighting stays bright, even, and shadow-light (default-style) so animation, hit-sound timing, and counter feedback are always legible. HUD hierarchy: a single top-right anchored label 'Hits: N' in a clean sans-serif, high-contrast against the background, updating with a small pop/flash or color pulse on increment so the feedback moment (animation swing -> sound -> counter tick) reads as one cohesive beat. No extraneous UI chrome; the space stays uncluttered so repetition and feedback remain the focus.

sources.behavior: Clones script.Parent into local var 'robo' at load. Runs an infinite wait(0) loop polling Humanoid.Health; when Health<1, waits 1s, clones the stored copy as 'robot', parents it into script.Parent.Parent, calls robot:makeJoints(), then removes the original dummy instance — an automatic respawn/reset of the target whenever its Humanoid health reaches zero.

integrationNotes: Disable or delete the Respawn Script (index 18) before integration so the dummy cannot self-destruct/reclone if any future damage source reduces Humanoid.Health; this is required to satisfy req-dummy-target's 'never resets' acceptance criteria, and is a proposed fix, not an applied one.

Torso Decal texture (rbxassetid://406436910) is unverified decorative content; no load/rights/appearance check has been performed.

plan.reason: The prior needs_more_evidence review identified that the bundled Respawn Script (index 18) polls Humanoid.Health and automatically clones/reparents the dummy while destroying the original whenever Health drops below 1, which directly contradicts req-dummy-target's mandatory acceptance criteria that the target 'never takes damage, ragdolls, resets, or respawns' and remains visually unchanged through repeated hits. This repair removes that script subtree entirely rather than stubbing it, since its only function is the forbidden reset/reclone behavior and it has no other useful logic worth preserving. All reusable mannequin geometry (Parts, Head, Torso, meshes, Humanoid) and the Torso decal are retained unmodified. No other component in this capture supplies hit-counting logic, so req-hit-counter remains dependent on the separately owned PunchServer integration task as already noted; that dependency is not resolved here and is restated in remainingIntegration.

removeSubtrees.reason: This Script clones script.Parent at load, then in an infinite polling loop checks Humanoid.Health<1 and, when true, waits 1s, reparents a cloned copy into script.Parent.Parent via makeJoints(), and removes the original — an automatic respawn/reset of the dummy. This is the exact behavior req-dummy-target forbids ('never...respawns', 'does not fall over or respawn'). The script contains no other logic (no hit detection, no counter, no decoration), so removing it loses no useful behavior while eliminating the disqualifying defect.

preservedBehavior: All static geometry Parts (indices 3,5,7,9,10,11,12) and their SpecialMesh children (4,6,8) are retained unmodified, preserving the mannequin's collidable shape for future touch/proximity hit-detection.

Head (13) and Torso (15) Parts with their SpecialMesh (14) and Decal (16, texture rbxassetid://406436910) are retained unmodified for visual appearance; the decal remains an unverified media reference pending later load/rights audit, not altered by this edit.

Humanoid (17) is retained so the model keeps a standard humanoid presence (e.g., for any future health-related UI or collision assumptions), but with the auto-respawn Script removed it no longer reacts to Health changes by cloning/destroying itself.
Overall Model/Training Dummy hierarchy (1, 2) and joint structure between parts is unchanged, so the dummy can still be anchored/placed at the approved position [0,3,12] as a single rigid assembly.
remainingIntegration: req-hit-counter and req-hit-detection still require the separately owned PunchServer component to add its own runtime touch/proximity or raycast listeners against this dummy's Parts (e.g., Torso/Head); no working hit-detection connection is established by this capture or this edit.

The Torso Decal texture (rbxassetid://406436910) remains an unverified media reference — its load, rights, and visual appearance have not been checked and must be confirmed during native/media verification before final acceptance.

With Humanoid (17) retained but no damage source in this game design (no player-damage mechanic per requirements), Health will not decrease during normal play; however, if any future script intentionally or accidentally sets Humanoid.Health<1, no respawn/reset code remains to react to it — this should be confirmed by native inspection rather than assumed.

Placement/anchoring at approximately [0,3,12] and CanCollide=true across all Parts must be confirmed in Studio; this capture provides geometry but placement is an integration task owned by targetDummySetup, not completed by this edit.
nativeTestPlan: In Studio, open the edited Training Dummy model and confirm index 18 (Script named 'Respawn') is no longer present under the model, with no other script remaining in its place.

Manually set the Humanoid's Health property to 0 in the Properties panel while the game is running in Studio and observe for at least 5 seconds that the dummy does NOT clone itself, does NOT reparent a duplicate, and the original instance is NOT removed — confirming the reset behavior is eliminated.
Verify all Parts (3,5,7,9,10,11,12,13,15) still have CanCollide=true and remain in their original relative positions/joints after the edit, with no visual change to the mannequin's appearance.

Confirm the Torso Decal (index 16, rbxassetid://406436910) still renders on the Torso part in Studio's 3D viewport as a basic visibility check; note that rights/appearance verification remains a separate deferred media check.

After PunchServer's touch/proximity listeners are implemented in the dependent component, native-test that repeated simulated hits against this dummy's Parts do not trigger any respawn/clone behavior and that the dummy remains a single persistent instance across many hits.
